name: N-acetyl-glucosamine
short: Few safety data. Healthy adults, 16-week placebo-controlled trial of a supplement containing it (size not given): no related adverse events. MS patients on glatiramer: an open trial called it safe.
text: Few safety data on N-acetyl-glucosamine taken by mouth were found: three human studies, two of them small and uncontrolled, and the abstract of the third does not give the number of participants. In a 16-week randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in healthy adults aged 23 to 64 taking a supplement containing it, no supplement-related adverse events were observed during or after the intervention. In an open-label, dose-escalation trial in people with multiple sclerosis who were also taking glatiramer acetate, 4 weeks of oral N-acetyl-glucosamine at 6 g (18 patients) or 12 g (16 patients) was reported as safe (the abstract does not give the dosing interval or say whether any patients took both doses); the abstract does not list adverse events, and the supplement also lowered blood levels of the anti-inflammatory signalling molecule IL-10 in a dose-dependent way. In an uncontrolled pilot study in 12 children with severe treatment-resistant inflammatory bowel disease who took it by mouth alongside their usual treatment, the authors described it as nontoxic; four of these children required surgical resection, which the abstract does not attribute to the supplement, and the authors said controlled trials are required. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
